newsitem.title: USA: Ford to develop hydrogen fuel cell vehicle.
newsitem.headline: Ford to develop hydrogen fuel cell vehicle.

text.p: Ford Motor Co on Monday said it would jointly develop a prototype hydrogen fuel cell vehicle with the U.S. Department of Energy.

The project, estimated to cost about $30 million, is associated with Ford's participation in the Partnership for a New Generation of Vehicles (PNGV), a collaborative effort to develop so-called ultra efficient vehicles. It involves the Big Three U.S. carmakers, the federal government and suppliers.
The Energy Department manages the fuel cell efforts of partnership. It has not been determined how the costs will be divided between Ford and the government.
The prototype will receive its power purely from hydrogen stored on board the vehicle. Chrysler Corp has announced a fuel cell project that uses both gasoline and hydrogen.
Ford said its vehicle may be ready for evaluation by 2000.

It is being developed under the umbrella of Ford's P2000 program. In addition to high fuel efficiency and low emission levels, P2000 vehicles are being designed to meet current family sedan comfort and performance standards.

The company said Ballard Power Systems Inc of Vancouver, British Columbia, Mechanical Technology Inc of New York and International Fuel Cells of Connecticut will ikely provide fuel cells for the project.
